harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Provisioned a LUKS1-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1 mounted at /srv/secure, set up to auto-unlock and mount at boot via a custom systemd oneshot unit (no crypttab loop-file support on systemd 229 / cryptsetup 1.6.6), and verified persistence across a real reboot with a changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Created a 2G sparse file /var/lib/secure/secure.img as LUKS backing store
Generated a random keyfile at /etc/cryptsetup-keys.d/secure.key (mode 400, root-only)
Ran cryptsetup luksFormat (LUKS1, aes-xts-plain64, 256-bit) and luksOpen against the file, backed automatically by /dev/loop0
Formatted the mapped device ext4 and mounted it at /srv/secure
Wrote /usr/local/sbin/secure-volume-mount.sh helper (idempotent start/stop: luksOpen + mount / umount + luksClose)
Wrote and enabled /etc/systemd/system/secure-volume.service (oneshot, RemainAfterExit, Before=local-fs.target) so the volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot
Wrote a marker.txt file with a timestamp+md5 to /srv/secure to prove data durability
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, mount/findmnt/df output, cryptsetup status, service enabled/active state
Triggered a native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming reconnection

Captured post-restart proof: new boot_id (changed), uptime reset to 0 min, secure-volume.service active, /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, cryptsetup status active, marker.txt content/md5 intact, and successfully appended new data post-reboot

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure
evidence.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat/luksOpen against secure.img, mkfs.ext4, and mount at /srv/secure all succeeded; mount and df confirm /dev/mapper/secure mounted at /srv/secure with 2.0G capacity

evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock and auto-mount configured for boot (pre-restart baseline)
evidence.summary: secure-volume.service written, enabled (symlinked into local-fs.target.wants), started successfully, and systemctl is-enabled/is-active confirm 'enabled'/'active' with mount and cryptsetup status healthy before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restart executed safely with returning acknowledgement
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued via backgrounded nohup so the exec call returned 'reboot command issued' before the SSH connection was dropped by the reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d (baseline) to 4991acb9-ee81-469a-b60c-6d80b031aed7 (post-restart), uptime reset to 0 minutes, and who -b shows a new boot time of Sep 29 09:08 vs original Jun 14 21:27

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact
evidence.summary: After reconnecting, secure-volume.service is active, /dev/mapper/secure is mounted at /srv/secure, cryptsetup status shows the LUKS device active, and marker.txt retains its pre-reboot content and md5 checksum; a post-reboot write also succeeded, confirming full read/write functionality
